conflicts.fact: Group 1 membership/placement of hydrogen and the set of elements in the Li, Na, K column
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 places H in group 1 (H, Li, Na, K) while saying Li, Na and K fall in one column; the fact sheet also gives H as group 1, so this is consistent, but Lesson 2 says 'Groups 1 to 18' columns in a 4-row grid of 20 elements, which is consistent. No real conflict.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the Lesson 5 teacher refers to as 'yesterday' for noble gas groups and what Lesson 5 says is learned in Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 teacher says 'Yesterday we saw that neon and argon sit in group 18 and do not react', which was Lesson 4 content (consistent). Lesson 6 teacher says 'Yesterday we learned that Ne and Ar are stable because their outer levels are full' (Lesson 5, consistent). No real conflict.

conflicts.fact: Rubidium prediction mentioned in Lesson 4 and Lesson 9 is not in the fact sheet
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 teacher asks 'Where in our model does the Rb prediction fit?' although no Rb prediction is in the Lesson 4 plan or map; Lesson 9 DQB mentions predicting an equation for rubidium as a new question.

conflicts.fact: When the products/equation for group 1 reaction with water are introduced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 Observe phase has learners name the products LiOH, NaOH, KOH solutions and test with indicator (equation left for Lesson 9), whereas Lesson 9 presents NaOH and H2 as a data card and says learners use Lesson 8 skills to write formulae, as if the products were new.
